decisionBoundary: This is a design proposal, not a preregistration, authorization, execution package, or provider approval.
hypothesis: Separating entity detection from relation predicate/endpoint decoding will make the dominant error source measurable and allow a gold-entity oracle ablation before any new live execution is considered.

stage1EntityDetection.input: source note text at runtime only
stage1EntityDetection.output: typed m3.v2 entity candidates with unique candidateId, label, half-open evidence span and confidence

stage2RelationDecoding.input: stage-1 entity candidates with candidateId/type/span plus source note text
stage2RelationDecoding.output: allowlisted predicate and directed source/target candidateId pairs with confidence

architecture.serverOwnedPostProcessing: Materialize and validate trigger-aware evidence after stage 2; model output cannot bypass endpoint or clause integrity rules.

oracleAblation.purpose: Identify whether relation failure remains when entity detection is removed from the causal path.

arms.interpretation: relation/predicate/endpoint/evidence ceiling conditional on perfect entity detection
metric and materializer integrity ceiling only; not a model quality arm

oracleAblation.requiredComparison: Compare gold-entities against predicted-entities on the same cases, runs, prompt and provider response custody model.
oracleAblation.rawPayloadPolicy: Do not persist raw provider payload or source text; persist sanitized per-case bucket counts, denominators, response digests and failure types only.
oracleAblation.reason: f11 did not persist predictions or per-relation buckets, so the gold-entity arm cannot be reconstructed from the closed report.

reviewQuestions: Is the stage-1 entity candidate contract sufficient for downstream endpoint identity and evidence evaluation?
Should stage 2 receive source text directly, or only a server-owned entity/context representation?
Are the proposed relation buckets and oracle arms sufficient to separate entity, predicate, endpoint and evidence failures?
What hard and slice thresholds should be preregistered for a future development-only run?
